claimBoundary: Transport is claim- and target-relative. Source evidence does not automatically become target truth, effect size, mechanism, authority or currentness.

BareinboimPearl2013.title: Meta-Transportability of Causal Effects: A Formal Approach
BareinboimPearl2013.boundary: formal causal transport under explicit source/target assumptions; not a generic Ordivon transport service

PearlBareinboim2015.title: External Validity: From Do-Calculus to Transportability Across Populations
PearlBareinboim2015.boundary: formal selection-diagram framework for population differences; requires causal assumptions

CorreaLeeBareinboim2022.title: Counterfactual Transportability: A Formal Approach
CorreaLeeBareinboim2022.boundary: formal counterfactual transport; non-identifiability can remain without additional assumptions

postures.name: STRUCTURAL_ANALOGY
postures.meaning: source preserves a useful distinction/question only; target mechanism/effect not claimed

postures.name: MECHANISM_SUPPORTED
postures.meaning: named causal mechanism believed shared with explicit changed-mechanism boundaries

postures.name: CALIBRATED_TARGET
postures.meaning: source mechanism plus bounded target probe covers decision-relevant moderators/differences

postures.name: TARGET_NATIVE
postures.meaning: target owner/population evidence directly answers the target query; source becomes support/prior/comparison

postures.name: NOT_TRANSPORTABLE_OR_UNKNOWN
postures.meaning: decision-relevant source-target mechanism difference is unresolved or formal assumptions are insufficient
